> I found a theremin quite difficult to make with oscillators etc. So instead I'm using a XIAO RP2040 to make a theremin. This is actually cheaper than the raw components of a theremin and simply detects hand movements as changes in capacitance which can then be translated to distinct pitch and volume frequencies.

### 2026-10-25 – Theremin #1

**1.5h**

Theremin #1

I spent a long time learning about theremins. To create a theremin you need an oscillator between a capacitor and inductor. To create these specific components, you could use JFET or amps for each pitch and volume antenna. My first attempt based off a YouTube video by Big Scott, but the oscillators they used were way too expensive. I tried a second prototype with raw components that utilised the inductor and capacitor more than pre-made oscillators. This type was much cheaper, although I spent a lot of time simulating Falstad and other similar websites. It was incredibly hard to simulate the JFETs, even in SPLICE (Kicad), and I had no other way of verifying if the project works. So, I revaluated, without appropriation and rather using a XIAO RP2350. On display are the more complex circuits I couldn't simulate, and thus I decided to not use.
